name: Tax Structuring and Planning
title: Tax Structuring and Planning
answer: Tax structuring and planning covers how AI businesses choose entity forms, locations, transfer pricing, IP ownership, and financing arrangements to manage tax obligations across jurisdictions. It includes pre-transaction planning for mergers, acquisitions, and reorganizations, as well as ongoing compliance with corporate income tax, VAT or GST, withholding, and digital services taxes. The page focuses on the tax consequences of AI-specific assets such as training data, model weights, and compute contracts. It describes common structures and their treatment rather than providing advice.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Tax structuring work runs on entity management databases, intercompany agreement repositories, transfer pricing documentation platforms, and tax provision software. Teams also pull actuals from general ledger and ERP systems to test scenarios. The site's corpus of 432 company pages and 352 merger and acquisition filings provides a reference set for comparing structures across the AI sector.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by mapping a company's legal entities, functions, assets, and risks to jurisdictions, then testing alternative holding and financing arrangements against local tax rules. Practitioners prepare functional analyses, benchmark intercompany margins, and model effective tax rates under different IP ownership and cost-sharing arrangements. For AI companies, this often involves valuing intangible assets such as algorithms and datasets and allocating profit to the entities that develop or exploit them. The process is iterative and relies on tax authority guidance, treaties, and case law.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Tax structuring carries risk from anti-avoidance rules, substance requirements, and disclosure regimes such as mandatory disclosure rules and country-by-country reporting. The provenance of a structure matters because tax authorities look at whether entities have real decision-making capacity, employees, and assets, not just contracts. The site tracks 210 compliance and regulation pages and 142 active AI lawsuits, which include disputes over transfer pricing and permanent establishment. This section outlines the risk areas without recommending a position.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Tax structuring for AI is moving toward greater transparency and real-time reporting, with tax authorities using data analytics to compare structures across companies. The OECD's two-pillar framework and unilateral digital services taxes are changing where profit is taxed, which affects how AI companies locate IP and sales functions. As AI-specific assets become more standardized, we expect more guidance on the valuation of training data and model weights. The site's 117 listed AI-related instruments may grow as new tax rules and treaties are issued.
